target_customer: Subprime US consumers who take short-term small-dollar loans and want to build credit
problem: Payday loans trap low-income borrowers in repeat high-cost debt and do not help them build credit. LendUp pitched a graduated ladder of cheaper loans and credit-building courses.
business_model: Direct online lender: interest and fees on small-dollar loans, later installment loans, credit cards and savings products, funded by equity and debt facilities

founders.name: Sasha Orloff
previous_startups: Later co-founded Mission Lane (LendUp spinout) and Puzzle.io, per the YC page
founders.background_notes: Background before LendUp not given on the sources opened.

founders.name: Jacob Rosenberg
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2013-11) says he previously worked at Zynga.

exit.reason: The CFPB announced on 2021-12-21 a proposed settlement under which LendUp Loans halts new loans and collections on certain outstanding loans, after a September 2021 suit over deceptive Ladder marketing and a 2016 order violation. Wind-down completion was reported for 2022.

technical_complexity.rationale: Instant data-driven underwriting on non-traditional data, credit bureau reporting and a gamified course ladder, built in-house; a standard but regulated fintech stack.

defensibility.rationale: State lending licenses and debt facilities took effort, but the underwriting and marketing idea were copyable, and the Ladder claim later became a legal liability.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent payday lenders did not copy it. Regulators, not incumbents, ended the business via CFPB actions in 2016, 2020 and 2021.

market_need_then: Payday lending was widely criticized as a debt trap and the TechCrunch 2013-11 launch coverage describes loans to people with poor or no credit; a Yahoo article from 2013-03 groups LendUp with other startups offering alternatives to payday loans.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-driven and consumer-friendly, framed as ladders not chutes

branding.brand_signature: The slogan Ladders Not Chutes and the LendUp Ladder tier program

brand_strength.rationale: The ladder metaphor was distinctive and drew press, but the CFPB found the Ladder claims deceptive, which turned the core brand promise into a liability.

outcome_analysis: LendUp raised large equity and debt amounts and grew to about 200 staff, spinning out Mission Lane. Its central brand claim, that repaying on time moved borrowers up a Ladder to cheaper loans, was found deceptive by the CFPB in 2016 and again in 2021, alongside a Military Lending Act judgment. The 2021 settlement halted new lending and collections, so regulation and legal exposure ended the business.
notes: Company website field is empty in the directory. Mission Lane spinout noted on YC page.
